title: SMTP authority boundaries and signed relay invariants
summary: SMTP transport, authentication attribution, message-signature verification, EMAIL_SEND authority, and ingress/egress policy are independent gates. Authentication alone never grants relay and the server never manufactures a user signature to make an unsigned message relayable.
invariants: No message signature means no outbound relay.
A valid message signature does not imply EMAIL_SEND authority.
The verified signer must match the attributed SMTP principal.
Signed plus EMAIL_SEND-authorized mail remains subject to egress deterministic and configured ML/LLM policy.
Inbound verified-signed mail routes to INBOX; unsigned or invalid-signature mail routes to INBOX-UNSIGNED unless stronger ingress policy rejects or quarantines it.
Signature evidence is projected before ingress and egress inspection so policy and models can use it without owning signature semantics.
Durability, queue presence, authentication, TLS, and instrumentation never become release authority.
Current LDAP consumer contract is active attributed IdentityDirectory principal plus explicit MAIL_READ/EMAIL_SEND; LDAP Bind or message signing never implies EMAIL_SEND.
procedure: For relay, re-verify the immutable message signature against the attributed principal.
Re-run deterministic egress inspection and configured model advisory.
Only then permit next-hop network transmission.

provenance.claim: Defines the relay, inbound-routing, durable/retry, MAS and RPC security invariants.
Executable implementation of signature evidence, relay-release validation, EMAIL_SEND authorization, ingress/egress inspection and event projection.
